text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=redwood-gateway — sudden increase in 5xx (5m avg 8.9%), p95 latency spike. Paging #incidents.

oncall-jules: ack. Pulling in traces and customer reports. Which region?

eng-sre-maya: appears localized to us-east-1 region starting 11:04 UTC. prefix_cache.eviction_rate jumped ~10x at 11:03, KV read errors appear immediately after: "kv: checksum mismatch" and "kv: incomplete segment read" in several gateway pods.

eng-runtime-raj: we rolled a TTL experiment this morning limited to us-east-1: cfg:ttl-experiment-20260316 that set prefix_cache.ttl=3s for a subset of service classes. Rollout id matches. That short TTL could cause hot-key churn.

oncall-jules: ok pause there. @deploy-bot can you revert cfg:ttl-experiment-20260316 -> cfg:prod-2026-03-15-2000 in us-east-1?

deploy-bot: Received rollback request. Initiating revert: cfg:ttl-experiment-20260316 -> cfg:prod-2026-03-15-2000 for region=us-east-1. Estimated convergence 60-120s. Posting status updates.

product-ops-sam: FYI CS queue just flagged 4 customers with streaming disconnects. Lina are they all paying customers?

cs-lina: yes, 4 that opened tickets; two flagged as priority accounts. I'm drafting an initial customer note.

eng-sre-maya: telemetry: KV p95 latency jumped to 2.8s, gateway p50->400ms, p95->1.7s. Many gateway pods showing repeated KV client retries, amplifying load. The checksum logs suggest write/read inconsistency possibly due to eviction during active rewrite/compaction.

eng-runtime-raj: while rollback is in-flight, recommend enabling prefix-cache.fail_open so cache errors don't block serving and enable short-duration bypass for heavy routes. Also consider soft rate limits to prevent retry storms.

oncall-jules: agree. Run both mitigations now.

eng-sre-maya: commands I'm running (ops console):

```
# fail open so cache faults don't cascade
redwoodctl services update gateway --set prefix_cache.fail_open=true --region=us-east-1
# set temporary bypass for streaming route
redwoodctl routes set /v1/stream --prefix_cache.bypass=true --duration=15m --region=us-east-1
# apply conservative per-org rate limit for streaming to break retry loops
redwoodctl limits update streaming.per_org_max=20 --duration=15m --region=us-east-1
```

eng-runtime-raj: good. I'm also going to pause background compaction on suspected shards until we stabilize. Command: `kvctl shard pause-compaction --shards=shard-2,shard-10 --region=us-east-1`

eng-sre-maya: logs: repeating message from node usrv-42: "kv: checksum mismatch for key prefix:v2:xyz123 during rewrite; read fallback succeeded from replica but with delay". Replica reads are slowing requests — contributing to 5xx and timeouts.

deploy-bot: Rollback converged in 64s for region=us-east-1. TTL restored to prod value. fail_open and route bypass applied to AZ-1/3; will continue rollout.

eng-sre-maya: post-mitigation numbers: 5xx dropped 8.9% -> 2.3% over 5m. KV p95 down to ~560ms. Still seeing intermittent checksum errors on two nodes in shard-10.

product-ops-sam: sending customer update: "We've reverted an experimental cache configuration and applied temporary mitigations to reduce errors. We're investigating storage consistency; we'll follow up within 60 minutes." Proceed with that copy?

cs-lina: send. I'll attach ticket numbers.

eng-runtime-raj: next steps: run verify-only scan on suspect shards to enumerate affected segments, `kvctl repair --verify --shards=shard-10`. If verify finds corruption, we should attempt targeted segment repair using replicas before considering snapshot restore.

eng-sre-maya: starting verify job now (job id verify-214159-1106). Running in low-cpu priority.

eng-sre-maya: small note — one host shows disk I/O errors around the time of the first checksum logs. Could be underlying node instability + eviction churn. We should consider isolating that host.

eng-runtime-raj: agree. Command to demote node to maintenance: `kvctl node annotate usrv-42 maintenance=true reason='observe-disk-errors'` and redirect writes away.

oncall-jules: go ahead and demote if you think it's necessary. Keep me posted.

eng-sre-maya: demoting node usrv-42 now. Also creating temporary read-only for shard-10 to prevent new writes during verification: `kvctl shard set-mode shard-10 read-only --reason='stabilize-after-eviction-storm'`

eng-runtime-raj: verify job update: 6m in — found 9 segments on shard-10 with checksum mismatches, several tied to segments rewritten during compaction windows. shard-2 clean.

eng-sre-maya: with rollback + fail_open + read-only + node demotion, traffic stabilized. But repairs needed for those 9 segments. Repair strategy: attempt targeted replica-fix for each segment using `kvctl repair --segments=seg-45,seg-46 --mode=repair --prefer-replica` and monitor. If repair fails, plan restore from snapshot for affected segments only.

product-ops-sam: customers asking if there's any risk to their stored data — what's the answer?

eng-runtime-raj: at the moment we have mismatches in segment checksums, meaning some replicas disagree. We prefer in-place repair using healthy replicas which normally preserves data. We'll only use snapshot restore if repair can't reconcile; we'll communicate steps if that happens.

cs-lina: relaying that to customers now — emphasize low probability of data loss and that engineers are attempting repairs.

eng-sre-maya: scheduling targeted repairs now but will hand off to night on-call for execution and monitoring. Repair job ids: staged as repair-214159-1125 (staged, waiting operational go).

eng-runtime-raj: additional post-incident controls proposal: 1) block prefix_cache.ttl < 10s in prod via rollout guard, 2) add a compaction-safety check that prevents compaction while eviction_rate > threshold, 3) automated fail-open when checksum errors spike. I'll write the RFC.

oncall-jules: handoff in 18m to @night-oncall-rua. Summary for handoff: rollback done, fail_open + route bypass + rate limits applied, node usrv-42 demoted, shard-10 set read-only, verify job found 9 bad segments, repairs staged. 5xx trending down and customer impact reduced. Postmortem owners: eng-sre-maya (lead), eng-runtime-raj (root cause & repair), product-ops-sam (customer comms).

night-oncall-rua: ack. I'll take the staged repair after verifying replication health and update the channel. Please drop links to dashboards and verify/repair job ids.

eng-sre-maya: dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/kv?region=us-east-1 ; verify id verify-214159-1106; repair id repair-214159-1125. Logs filtered: https://logs.redwood.internal/q=checksum+shard-10

deploy-bot: additional note: autoscaler paused for gateway pods in us-east-1 to avoid scale churn while repairs are ongoing.

product-ops-sam: prepping customer follow-up template for postmortem. Will coordinate with eng leads.

incident-bot: Incident MITIGATED -> Monitoring. Duration to mitigation ~12 minutes. Root symptom: 5xx spike caused by prefix-cache eviction storm and subsequent KV checksum mismatches during concurrent rewrite. Actions taken: rollback TTL experiment, enabled fail_open and bypass, demoted suspect node, set shard read-only, verify+repair staged.

night-oncall-rua: taking over. Will run repair-214159-1125 after replication checks, will report back with results or escalate to storage team.
